text:
Vegas arrives in Buffalo three days after beating Detroit 2-1, a game the Golden Knights trailed in the third period before Trevor Connelly scored the winner with 1:42 left. They're 3-1-1 in their last five and still without Parker Wotherspoon. Buffalo is 4-1-0 over the same stretch after a 5-2 win over Columbus on Friday, though Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk are out. Rasmus Dahlin plays his 600th NHL game, one that matters in a building where Jack Eichel is the former franchise player.

The teams look close on paper. At five on five, Vegas has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games and Buffalo 50%, so there's little between them. Our model makes it 3.16 to 2.93 for Vegas. Buffalo has taken 4.1 penalties a game, and Vegas is generating 0.72 power play expected goals a game. In net, projected starters Carter Hart and Colten Ellis are both above average this season in goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stopped beyond what the chances should have allowed): Hart at +2.1, Ellis at +2.3. Last season, Hart was at -4.4 and Ellis at +2.2.

Eichel gives Vegas a 76% chance of a point by our numbers, and a reporter posted this week that Vegas has been generating plenty of chances. Victor Olofsson, drafted by Buffalo in 2014, is on a five-game point streak with six points. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson has a 37% chance to score and is one assist from 200 career assists.
